prerequisites: General requirements for the Master's Degree in Industrial Engineering.
It is not advised to take this course before having completed the previous semester.

learning_outcomes.text: Conduct research, development, and innovation in products, processes, and methods.
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students should possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Be able to work in a group through effective communication.
Be able to define, refocus, and meet system design specifications.
Be able to respond to problems or unforeseen events that arise during development.
Know the current state of robotics and its foreseeable evolution.
Understand the role of robotics within Industry 4.0.
Analyze and understand the technologies involved in a robotic system.
Know the fields in which robotics is expected to make breakthrough contributions.

syllabus_topics: Conferences and meetings: experts will present case studies and general topics related to robotics.
Technical visits: guided visits to real robotic installations for analysis and subsequent discussion.
Analysis of robotic systems from the Systems Engineering perspective.

assessment_methods.method: Formal aspects of document presentation (spelling, expression, explanation of ideas, graphics)
Student involvement and participation in discussions (interesting contributions)
Active interest in exchanging ideas, initiative in finding alternative solutions, critical capacity, reasoned contributions
Fluency and rigor in handling concepts, effective information exchange, clear, concise, and rigorous responses to questions during presentations

assessment_rules: Assessment will consider all group tutorials and participatory activities. Aspects such as formal quality of document presentation, student involvement in discussions, active interest in idea exchange and critical capacity, and fluency and rigor in presentations will each account for up to 25% of the final grade. For extraordinary examinations and differentiated assessment, the same evaluation system will be followed.
bibliography: Documentation provided by companies, institutions, and articles from major specialized robotics journals (in English).
Complementary information will be managed through the Virtual Campus and the dedicated website, analisis.dieecs.com
